sentences.text:
The petitioner has filed this petition being aggrieved by the arbitral award passed by the Special Deputy Commissioner/Arbitrator, Bengaluru Urban District, Bengaluru, in No.
LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR/62/2011-12 dated 16.03.2021 in respect of Sy. No.59/21(P)2/20A CMC Khatha No. 36/36 of Byatarayanapura village, Yelahanka Hobli, Bengaluru North Addl. Taluka, Bengaluru Urban District.

.2. The definite case of the petitioner is that the property bearing Sy. No.59/21(P)2/20A CMC Khatha No. 36/36 measuring 992 Sq. Meters of Byatarayanapura village has been acquired under Gazette notification No. S.O. No.1874 (E) dated 30.07.2010.
Prior to that Preliminary Notification issued under S.O. No.3159(E) A.P. No.195/2021 dated 09.12.2009.
Subsequently the respondent No.3/LAO has awarded a total sum of Rs.95,42,636/- as compensation for 1618 Sq. feet of the land belongs to the petitioner.
The petitioner received the same under protest and filed an application for enhancing the compensation.
Accordingly, the said application taken by the respondent No. 3 for consideration.
.3. In the said petition, the respondent No.2 filed statement of objection stating that the contention urged by the petitioner are baseless and the same are made without any substance.
The petitioner has not produced any relevant documents to justify his claim for enhanced compensation and the claim of the petitioner cannot be sustained in law.
Hence, question of enhancement of compensation will not arise and the claim of the petitioner is liable to be dismissed by the respondent No.2.

Accordingly, prayed to dismiss the reference.
. 4 . T h e r e a f t e r , t h e A r b i t r a t o r h o l d a n i n q u i r y a n d p a s s e d c o m m o n o r d e r i n

Being aggrieved by the impugned Arbitral Award, the petitioner filed this petition under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, setting up the following :
:GROUNDS:
The petitioner claims that the amount fixed by the respondent no . 3 was unfair and the respondent No. 1 while enhancing the compensation have not taken into consideration about the market value and the other necessary facts determine the fair compensation.

The award passed by the respondent No. 3 by fixing Rs. 1,618 per Sq.
feet is unjust and against to the provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

The respondent No.1 totally denied all the grounds claimed by the petitioner in the petition.

The Arbitrator/ respondent No. 3 passed the award after giving full opportunity of hearing to the petitioner by considering the material evidence on record for enhancement of compensation together with all other statutory benefits available under the LA Act in accordance with law and prayed for dismissal of the petition.
.7. The respondent No.1 appeared before the Court through DGP.
The respondents No.2 and 3 appeared before the Court through their Advocate.
The entire records in LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR/62/2011-12 dated 16.03.2021 secured from the Arbitrator.

.8. On the basis of above, the points for consideration are as under:
1) Whether the impugned award of the Arbitrator/SLAO is against law, fact, evidence and probabilities of the case and liable to be intervened by this Court?
2) What order or award?
.9.
Heard the arguments.

Perused the materials on record, on that basis my findings on the above points are as under:
Point No.1 : In the negative Point No.2 : As per final order, for the following:
REASONS .10.
POINT No.1:
Before proceeding further in this case, it is relevant to note an admitted and undisputed facts in this case.

The petitioner K.R. Geetha is an owner of the property bearing Sy. No.1(P)2/20A CMC Khatha No. 36/36 of Byatarayanapura village, measuring to an extent of 992 Sq. meters and the said property has been acquired for widening of NH-7 under Preliminary A.P.
No.195/2021 Notification dated 09.12.2009 and Final Notification dated 02.07.2010,
that has been published in the official Gazette on 02.07.2010, is an admitted fact.

It is also an admitted and undisputed fact in this case that the respondent No.2/Special Land Acquisition and Competent Authority of National Highways Authority of India being a SLAO determined the compensation at Rs. 1,618/- per Sq. feet for the acquired land for BDA/BMRDA sites.

entities.text: Special Land Acquisition and Competent Authority of National Highways Authority of India
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: It is also admitted and undisputed fact that a sum of Rs.95,42,636/- and Rs. 15,18,098/- towards building which includes security room, office building DVAR Block paving, MS gate, compound of CCB compound wall, BBM etc. was disbursed to the petitioner as compensation.

.11. Subsequent to the receipt of compensation or passing of the award, the petitioner K.R. Geetha filed an application before the respondent No.3 claiming that she is entitled for enhancement of compensation claiming that the land would fetch more than Rs. 6,500/- per Sq. feet as on 08.02.2012.

On basis of the said application, the Geetha K R vs The Special Deputy Commissioner And ... on 29 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92247348/
3 A.P. No.195/2021 respondent No.3 hold an inquiry and passed common order in LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR-62/2011-12 dated 16.03.2021.

entities.text: Geetha K R vs The Special Deputy Commissioner
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The respondent No.3 in its order enhanced the compensation at Rs3,606/- per Sq. feet.

As per petition averment at para No. 7, the respondent No. 3 / LAO / project director has fixed the compensation at Rs.
1,618/- per Sq. feet and that has been enhanced by the Arbitrator / Special Deputy Commissioner /
respondent No. 1 by adding Rs.3,606/- per Sq. feet.
if this pleading is accepted, then it has to be accepted that the respondent No. 1/ Arbitrator fixed compensation at Rs. 5,224/- per Sq. feet.

Further at this juncture, it is relevant to note that as per petition averments, the petitioner claims that the compensation fixed by respondent No.1 is Rs.95,42,636/- for acquired land including Rs.
15,18,098/- for the building etc., and that has been enhanced to the tune of Rs. 3,89,28,579/-.

Of course the petitioner claimed that the market value of the acquired land is more than Rs. 6,500/-
per Sq. feet, but no documents have been placed before the court to A.P. No.195/2021 substantiate the said contention.
The materiel on record sufficiently shows that the Arbitrator constrained all the material before it, properly assess the market value as per the order.
When the petitioner fails to make out any ground to show that the award passed by the Arbitrator is arbitrary or against the provision of law, certainly such order cannot be interfered by this Court.

Therefore, this Court is of the humble opinion that the petitioner has failed to make out sufficient grounds to intervene with the order passed by the respondent No.1 and the order of the respondent no.1 is in accordance with the law and said order is in accordance with law by considering all the material documents placed before the Arbitrator.
Accordingly, the point No.1 is held in the negative.
.12. Point No.2:
In view of my above finding, I proceed to pass the following.
ORDER Petition filed under Section 34 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 by the petitioner is hereby dismissed.

Consequently, the impugned award passed by the respondent No.3 in case No.LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR/62/2011-12 dated 16.03.2021 in respect of Sy.
No.59/21(P)2/20A CMC Khatha No. 36/36 of Byatarayanapura village, Yelahanka Hobli, Bengaluru North Addl. Taluka, Bengaluru Urban District is confirmed.
Parties to bear their own cost.
Send back the records.

pronounced in open Court on this the 29 th day of May, 2024) (PADMA PRASAD) II Addl. City Civil and Sessions Judge, & Spl. Judge, Bangalore.
